tools.name: estimate
tools.description:
Price a question before asking it, check your credits, and look up what you can ask for: ready-made templates, interest audiences and targeting options. Never spends. Call quote first, and when a person is present show them the price and time together before you ask.

Pass action: one of quote, balance, templates, audiences, targeting. Each action takes only its own arguments.
- quote: Price a question before asking it: credits, the price, how long it will take and any fixes it needs. Never spends. Call this first, and when a person is present show them the price and time together before you ask. Arguments: question (required), currency. Read-only; needs questions:write.
- balance: Credits available, credits reserved by live questions, and what is left under this connection's daily spend cap. Check before asking something large. No other arguments. Read-only; needs account:read.
- templates: Ready-made questions at a fixed price. Pick one, fill in its options and pass its question to ask (action ask) with template_id. No sign-in needed. No other arguments. Read-only; no sign-in needed.
- audiences: Interest audiences: panels of heads who proved they ride, own, run or buy something (for example UK commuter cyclists). Put an id in question.audience to ask one instead of targeting; the price is the audience's at the minimum grade. No sign-in needed; signed in, private audiences your team sponsors are listed too. Arguments: q, country. Read-only; no sign-in needed.
- targeting: Who can answer: countries with the languages their heads read and pool size bands by tier, the age bands and genders heads declare, and the tag catalog you can target at any tier. Use the codes and tag ids in question.targeting. No sign-in needed. Arguments: language. Read-only; no sign-in needed.

action.description: What to do. One of: quote, balance, templates, audiences, targeting. Each action takes its own arguments; see the tool description.

go_above.description: The line, as a share of Yes from 0.5 to 0.95 in whole percentages (0.6 is 60%). The result is a go when the whole 95% range on the Yes share is above it.

min_answers.description: Answers needed before the result can be a go or a no go: at least 5, at most n. Default 80% of n, rounded down.

go_rule.description: Go or no go: for an approval-style question ("Would you sign up?", "Is this label clear enough to ship?"), go when Yes clears the line you set. The result then carries a verdict: go, no_go, or unclear (too few answers, or the range crosses the line). Set it before asking; it cannot move once the question is live. Costs nothing extra. On yes_mostly_no, Mostly counts as half a Yes. It is how these heads answered against your line, not a fact.

oneOf.description: Yes or No. Binary. For a middle answer, use yes_mostly_no. Add go_rule to get a go or a no go when Yes clears your line.

tools.name: ask
tools.description:
Ask verified people a question and get their answers back as a distribution (ask), ask your own audience several questions behind one link (set), upload an image a question can show, or build a link for a person to press Ask themselves. ask and set spend credits within this connection's daily cap and need a fresh UUID as idempotency_key; retrying with the same key never charges twice. Uploading an image and building a link cost nothing. Ask about preferences and first impressions, never facts; read 50heads://guide for wording.

Pass action: one of ask, set, upload_image, build_link. Each action takes only its own arguments.
- ask: Ask verified people a question and get their answers back as a distribution. Spends credits, within this connection's daily cap. Needs a fresh UUID as idempotency_key; retrying with the same key never charges twice. Returns a task to wait on, or on older hosts a question_id: then call results with action wait. If the organization holds asks over a limit for a person's approval, status is pending_approval and the task is input_required until someone approves at approval.approve_url; a denial ends it as refused_by_policy. Call estimate (action quote) first. Ask about preferences and first impressions, never facts; read 50heads://guide for wording. For a yes-or-no decision, add question.go_rule to get a go or a no go when Yes clears your line. Arguments: question (required), idempotency_key (required), template_id, variants, then, project_id, labels, external_ref. Changes something; needs questions:write.
- set: Publish two to ten questions behind one link for people you know (your audience): they answer each in turn in the browser, about five seconds each, with no account. Each question keeps its own results (results, action get, per question_id); 5 credits an accepted answer, not verified by 50heads. Spends credits, within this connection's daily cap. Needs a fresh UUID as idempotency_key; retrying with the same key never charges twice. For one question use action ask with answered_by "private"; for verified heads use action ask. Arguments: questions (required), idempotency_key (required), max_answers, open_for_days, shown_as, public_results, project_id, labels. Changes something; needs questions:write.
- upload_image: Puts an image into 50heads so a question can show it: base64 bytes (data), or a public https link to copy (image_url). Returns image_url to use in a question's options or stimulus. JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB; metadata is stripped and heads never load your server. Costs nothing. Arguments: image_url, data, content_type. Changes something; needs questions:write.
- build_link: A link to the 50heads portal with a question already filled in, for a person to check and ask themselves: text, type, options and images, heads, tier, countries and tags, or a template, follow-up or re-ask. Nothing is asked or spent. Use it when a person should press Ask, or to hand a draft to a colleague. No sign-in needed. Arguments: draft, template_id, follow_up_of, reask, bulk. Read-only; no sign-in needed.

tools.name: results
tools.description:
Read what people answered: the results so far (get), wait for them (wait), single answers (answers), a file (export) and your list of questions (list). Read-only. Check list before asking again: a recent answer may already cover it.

Pass action: one of get, wait, answers, export, list. Each action takes only its own arguments.
- get: The results so far for a question: status, how many answered, the share per option, the winner, margin and confidence, a verdict (go, no_go or unclear) for a yes-or-no question asked with a go_rule, who beats whom (head_to_head) for ranking and pairwise, and a 95% range on each pairwise win share, breakdowns by country, tier, age band, gender and tag (groups of 5 or more), taps and hot spots for click tests, the share per reaction, any written answers and reasons (translated into the account's language), and a summary of them (themes, sentiment, a takeaway). Each answer carries choice (option indexes) and the result a cohort_hash: the same value means the same kind of audience was asked, so results can be grouped across questions. Filter by option, tier, country, age_band, gender or keyword to read one group. Does not wait: while the question is live it returns a partial result. Arguments: question_id (required), currency, option, tier, country, age_band, gender, keyword. Read-only; needs questions:read.
- wait: Waits on the server until the question is answered, or min_answers are in, or the timeout passes (default 300 s, most 600), then returns the results. One call instead of polling. If it comes back still live, call it again. Arguments: question_id (required), min_answers, timeout_seconds. Read-only; needs questions:read.
- answers: Individual answers to a question, newest first, a page at a time: the option picked (and choice, as option indexes), any written answer or reason, tier and an attestation_ref. Filter by option, tier, country, age band or a keyword (q); pass next_cursor for the next page. Answers never identify a head. Arguments: question_id (required), option, tier, country, age_band, gender, q, limit, cursor. Read-only; needs questions:read.
- export: A question's results as a file: csv (every answer, with the same filters as action answers), jsonl (the same answers as JSON lines, one object per answer with option indexes and the cohort hash, for scripts and model training), pdf (a one-page report) or png (the result card). Returns the file in the reply when it is small enough, and its API url. Arguments: question_id (required), format, option, tier, country, age_band, gender, q. Read-only; needs questions:read.
- list: Your recent questions with status and answer counts, newest first. Check here before asking again: a recent answer may already cover it. Filter by project, label, your own external reference, bookmark or set (ask, action set); archived questions are left out unless you ask for them. Arguments: status, since, limit, cursor, project_id, label, external_ref, archived, bookmarked, set_id. Read-only; needs questions:read.

tools.name: questions
tools.description:
Change one question you asked: stop it (cancel), ask more heads (add_heads), report an answer that looks off (flag_answer), or file it into a project, label it, archive it, bookmark it or set your own reference (file). cancel stops a live question and refunds the heads who have not answered.

Pass action: one of cancel, add_heads, flag_answer, file. Each action takes only its own arguments.
- cancel: Stops a live question. Heads who have not answered are refunded; answers already given are kept and paid for. Safe to call twice. Arguments: question_id (required). Destructive; needs questions:write.
- add_heads: Asks more heads the same question, with the same targeting, and merges their answers into the same result. Spends credits at the question's per-answer price, within this connection's daily cap. Needs a fresh UUID as idempotency_key; retrying with it never charges twice. Arguments: question_id (required), n (required), idempotency_key (required). Changes something; needs questions:write.
- flag_answer: Reports one answer that looks off-topic, low effort, abusive or automated, by its attestation_ref from results (actions answers or get). 50heads reviews it; an upheld flag removes the answer and refunds it. Flagging the same answer again changes nothing. Arguments: question_id (required), attestation_ref (required), reason (required), note. Changes something; needs questions:write.
- file: Files one of your questions: moves it into a project (project_id, or null to take it out), replaces its labels (up to 10), archives or unarchives it, bookmarks it, or sets your own external_ref. Send only what should change. external_ref is set once: the same value again is fine, a different one is refused. A live question must be canceled before it is archived. Costs nothing and returns the question as results (action list) shows it. Arguments: question_id (required), project_id, labels, archived, bookmarked, external_ref. Changes something; needs questions:write.

tools.name: projects
tools.description:
Keep questions findable: list, create, update (rename, describe, archive) and delete projects, and list the labels on your questions. A project groups questions; delete removes the project only, never its questions. File a question with questions (action file) or with project_id and labels when asking.

Pass action: one of list, create, update, delete, labels. Each action takes only its own arguments.
- list: Your projects: groups of questions with a name and a description, bookmarked first, each with how many questions are filed in it. Archived projects are left out unless include_archived is true. A key made for a team lists the team's projects. Use a project_id with ask (actions ask and set), questions (action file) or results (action list). Arguments: include_archived. Read-only; needs questions:read.
- create: Makes a project to group questions, with a name and an optional description. Costs nothing. File questions in it with project_id on ask (actions ask and set), or later with questions (action file). Calling it twice makes two projects. Arguments: name (required), description. Changes something; needs questions:write.
- update: Renames a project, changes its description, or archives it (archived: true) or brings it back (false). Archiving a project leaves its questions as they are. Costs nothing. Arguments: project_id (required), name, description, archived. Changes something; needs questions:write.
- delete: Deletes a project for good. Its questions are not deleted: they keep their answers, results, labels and bookmarks, and are no longer in any project. Nothing is charged or refunded. To keep the project but hide it, use action update with archived: true instead. Confirm with the person first. Arguments: project_id (required). Destructive; needs questions:write.
- labels: The labels on your questions, most used first, with how many questions carry each. Use one as label in results (action list), or reuse it in questions (action file) or ask. No other arguments. Read-only; needs questions:read.

tools.name: webhooks
tools.description:
Webhook endpoints that 50heads sends signed events to: list, create, update, rotate the signing secret, test, read deliveries and recent events, replay a delivery, and delete. Question events carry question ids, status, labels, projects and the results summary, so only use an address the person owns and has asked for. Read 50heads://webhook-events for the event types.

Pass action: one of list, create, update, rotate_secret, test, deliveries, events, replay, delete. Each action takes only its own arguments.
- list: The webhook endpoints of this account (personal, or the team the connection acts for): address, events, filter, whether each is on, and how the last delivery went. Secrets are masked. No other arguments. Read-only; needs webhooks:read.
- create: Adds a webhook endpoint: 50heads then sends the chosen events, signed, to that https address as they happen. Question events carry question ids, status, labels, projects and the results summary, so only use an address the person owns and has asked for, and confirm it with them first. The signing secret is in this reply only; give it to the person to store with the receiver. Read 50heads://webhook-events for the event types. Arguments: url (required), events (required), description, filter. Changes something; needs webhooks:write.
- update: Changes a webhook endpoint's address, events, description or filter (filter null clears it), or pauses it (enabled false) and turns it back on (enabled true), also after it was switched off for failing. A new address gets this account's events: confirm it with the person first. Arguments: id (required), url, events, description, enabled, filter. Changes something; needs webhooks:write.
- rotate_secret: Makes a new signing secret for a webhook endpoint and returns it once, in this reply only. The old secret keeps signing beside the new one for overlap_hours (default 24, up to 168), so the receiver can switch without missing a delivery; 0 cuts over at once and deliveries fail until the receiver has the new secret. Arguments: id (required), overlap_hours. Changes something; needs webhooks:write.
- test: Sends a signed webhook.test event to one endpoint now and says how the receiver answered. Use it after action create, a change of address or a secret rotation. Arguments: id (required). Changes something; needs webhooks:write.
- deliveries: The latest 100 webhook deliveries, newest first, with state, the receiver's status, attempts and the last error. Filter by endpoint_id or state; state failed lists the ones that ran out of retries, which action replay sends again. Arguments: endpoint_id, state. Read-only; needs webhooks:read.
- events: The latest events of one type in this account, newest first (limit 1 to 25, default 3), each exactly as a delivery's body carries it: id, type, createdAt, apiVersion and data. Events are kept whether or not an endpoint listens, so use this for a sample payload when writing a receiver, or to catch up on events by id. Arguments: type (required), limit. Read-only; needs webhooks:read.
- replay: Sends a delivery's event again as a new delivery, with the same event id and body, signed with the endpoint's current secrets. Receivers that drop duplicate event ids ignore it if they already have it. Arguments: delivery_id (required). Changes something; needs webhooks:write.
- delete: Deletes a webhook endpoint: no more events go to it, and it cannot be brought back. To stop deliveries for a while, use action update with enabled false instead. Confirm with the person first. Arguments: id (required). Destructive; needs webhooks:write.

Read-only view of the organization this key or app acts in: the organization (get), its verified domains, SCIM provisioning, one member's sessions, service accounts, and the Slack workspaces, Microsoft Teams tenants and Zapier accounts added to the account (apps). Changes are made in the portal, never here.

- get: The organization of the workspace this key or app acts in: its name, your role, its workspaces, verified domains, whether single sign-on is set up or required, whether SCIM provisioning is connected, its sign-in rules, and whether service accounts are available. Needs organization:read. Read-only: changes are made in the portal (Settings, Organization). No other arguments. Read-only; needs organization:read.
- domains: The email domains the organization has added, each with its state (pending, verified, warning, failed) and the DNS TXT record that proves it. Organization admins only; needs organization:read. Read-only. No other arguments. Read-only; needs organization:read.
- scim: Whether the organization's identity provider (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID) provisions people through SCIM: the base URL, how many people and groups it has sent, the default role, and its tokens (labels and prefixes, never the tokens). Organization admins only; needs organization:read. Read-only: tokens are made and replaced by a person in the portal. No other arguments. Read-only; needs organization:read.
- member_sessions: Where one person in the organization is signed in: each live web or app session with how it started (email, passkey, single sign-on…), its country and when it was last used. Organization admins only; needs members:read. Read-only: signing someone out happens in the portal, or with members:write through the API. Arguments: user_id (required). Read-only; needs members:read.
- service_accounts: The organization's service accounts: machine identities it owns (not a person), each with its workspace, scopes, daily and per-question caps in credits, today's spend, how it signs in and when it last got a token. tools.name: help
tools.description:
Search the 50heads help center (search), send feedback or a problem to support (feedback), check whether 50heads is working and whether asking is paused (status), or see who this connection acts as, with its scopes, caps and rate limits (whoami). Call whoami first when something is refused, and status when calls fail. search, feedback and status need no sign-in; whoami reads the account.

Pass action: one of search, feedback, status, whoami. Each action takes only its own arguments.
- search: Searches the 50heads help center (asking, results, credits and billing, verification, the API and MCP) and returns the best articles with links. Use it to answer a person's question about how 50heads works. No sign-in needed. Arguments: query (required), locale, limit. Read-only; no sign-in needed.
- feedback: Sends feedback or a problem to 50heads support as a ticket; a person replies by email. Use it when something about 50heads or this server did not work, or to suggest something. Signed in, the reply goes to the account's email; otherwise add email. Arguments: message (required), subject, kind, email. Changes something; no sign-in needed.
- status: Whether 50heads is working right now, and whether asking, answering, MCP asking or buying credits is paused. Check it when calls fail or results stop filling, and do not ask while asking is paused (nothing is charged while paused). No sign-in; costs nothing. No other arguments. Read-only; no sign-in needed.
- whoami: Who this connection acts as (a person or a service account, email masked), its scopes, its daily and per-question caps and today's spend, the account it spends from (personal or a team, with the role there), the organization where one is switched on, and the rate limits with what is used now. action.description: What to do. One of: search, feedback, status, whoami. Each action takes its own arguments; see the tool description.

query.description: What you want to know, in a few words. (Used by: search.)

locale.description: Help center language. Default en-gb. (Used by: search.)

message.description: The feedback or problem, in plain words. Leave out personal data about other people. (Used by: feedback.)

email.description: Only when not signed in, so support can reply. (Used by: feedback.)

instructions: 50heads asks verified people a five-second question and shows what they think. Use it for human preferences and first impressions, never for facts. Call estimate (action quote) first and show the price and time together when a person is present; then ask (action ask) with a fresh UUID as idempotency_key, and wait on the task (or results, action wait). Read 50heads://guide for how to word a good question. Keep questions findable with projects (projects: list, create; labels) and questions, action file. When a call is refused call help (action whoami); when calls fail check help (action status). We don't use your questions, the answers you buy or the reasons heads write to train AI models, and we don't sell them.
